title: Euler liars: the half and quarter cases
summary: Odd squarefree composites with φ(n)/2 or φ(n)/4 Euler liars are Carmichael numbers or of the form p(2p−1).
source: A. Alcantarilla Sánchez, J. Cottaar, T. Lange, B. de Weger, "Ours go to 211: Euler pseudoprimes to 47 prime bases (from Carmichael numbers)", arXiv:2602.21840v1 (25 February 2026), the conjecture closing the appendix on "Sophie Germinus pseudoprimes".
label: lean
first_by: The half case is in a 2011 paper (Di Biagio, arXiv:1109.3596). The quarter case is reported to be stated as a theorem on the web page of the paper's own authors, which says a proof exists and a write-up is in preparation; that page could not be opened from here and its content is as reported by a public record. No earlier machine-checked proof was found.
